sentences.zh: 昭忠祠諭曰：「周禮有司勛之官，凡有功者，書名太常，祭於大烝。

translations.literal: Regarding the Temple of Manifest Loyalty, an edict stated: "In the Rites of Zhou there is the office of Director of Merits; all who have merit have their names recorded in the Court of Imperial Sacrifices and are offered sacrifice at the great seasonal offering.
translations.idiomatic: On the Temple of Manifest Loyalty, an imperial edict declared: "The Rites of Zhou provide for a Director of Merits: anyone who has performed meritorious service has his name entered in the Court of Imperial Sacrifices and receives offerings at the great seasonal sacrifice.

sentences.zh: 祭法，『以死勤事則祀之』。

translations.literal: The Rules of Sacrifice say, "Those who die in diligent service to their duties shall be sacrificed to."
translations.idiomatic: The Rules of Sacrifice state that "those who die in the diligent discharge of their duties shall receive sacrificial rites."

sentences.zh: 於以崇德報功，風厲忠節。

translations.literal: By this virtue is exalted and merit requited, and loyalty and integrity are encouraged as a model.
translations.idiomatic: Thus virtue is honored and merit rewarded, and loyalty and integrity are held up as an example to inspire others.

sentences.zh: 自太祖創業後，將帥之臣，守土之官，沒身捍國，良可嘉憫。

translations.literal: Since the founding of the enterprise by the Taizu, generals and commanders, and officials who guarded the realm, have given their lives in defense of the state—truly worthy of praise and compassion.
translations.idiomatic: Since the Taizu founded the dynasty, countless generals and regional officials have laid down their lives for the state—deeds truly worthy of commemoration and compassion.

sentences.zh: 允宜立祠京邑，世世血食。

translations.literal: It is altogether fitting to establish temples in the capital so that they may receive blood offerings generation after generation.
translations.idiomatic: It is altogether fitting to establish temples in the capital where they may receive sacrificial offerings in perpetuity.

sentences.zh: 其偏裨士卒殉難者，亦附祀左右。

translations.literal: Those subordinate officers and soldiers who died in the calamity shall also be enshrined in attendance on either side.
translations.idiomatic: Subordinate officers and soldiers who died in the line of duty shall likewise be enshrined in subsidiary positions on either side.

sentences.zh: 褒崇表闡，俾遠近觀聽，勃然可生忠義之心，並為立傳垂永久。」

translations.literal: By honoring and exalting them and making their deeds manifest, so that observers near and far may behold and be stirred to loyalty and righteousness, and moreover by composing biographies to endure forever."
translations.idiomatic: By honoring them publicly and making their deeds known, observers near and far may be stirred to loyalty and righteousness; biographies shall also be composed so that their memory endures."

sentences.zh: 於是建祠崇文門內，歲春、秋仲月，諏吉，遣官致祭。

translations.literal: Thereupon a temple was built inside Chongwen Gate; each year in the second month of spring and autumn, an auspicious day was chosen and an official was dispatched to perform the sacrifice.
translations.idiomatic: Accordingly a temple was erected inside Chongwen Gate. Each year in the second month of spring and of autumn, an auspicious day was chosen and an official was sent to conduct the sacrifice.

sentences.zh: 王公大臣位正殿，陳案七，羊一、豕一。

translations.literal: For princes, dukes, and great ministers in the main hall, seven tables were set out, with one sheep and one pig.
translations.idiomatic: In the main hall, where princes, dukes, and senior ministers were enshrined, seven offering tables were laid, each with one sheep and one pig.

sentences.zh: 左三案，共羊豕各一。

translations.literal: On the left, three tables shared one sheep and one pig in all.
translations.idiomatic: On the left, three tables shared one sheep and one pig among them.

sentences.zh: 右如之。

translations.literal: On the right it was the same.
translations.idiomatic: The arrangement on the right was the same.

sentences.zh: 每案素帛一、爵三、果盤五。

translations.literal: On each table were one piece of plain silk, three libation cups, and five trays of fruit.
translations.idiomatic: Each table bore one piece of plain silk, three libation vessels, and five trays of fruit.

sentences.zh: 諸臣位兩配樓暨後正室，各設案五，兩廡各設案三，皆羊豕各一，為通數。

translations.literal: For the various officials in the two side halls and the rear main chamber, five tables were set at each place; in each of the two wings three tables were set—all with one sheep and one pig each as the standard allotment.
translations.idiomatic: Officials enshrined in the two side halls and the rear main chamber each had five offering tables; the two wings each had three tables, every table furnished with one sheep and one pig as the standard offering.

sentences.zh: 兵士附祀，案三十有六，案設豕肉一盤、爵三、果品二。

translations.literal: For soldiers enshrined in attendance, there were thirty-six tables; on each table were one platter of pork, three libation cups, and two kinds of fruit.
translations.idiomatic: Soldiers enshrined in subsidiary positions had thirty-six tables in all; each table held one platter of pork, three libation vessels, and two kinds of fruit.

sentences.zh: 太常卿承祭，配樓後室司官分獻。

translations.literal: The Director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices presided over the sacrifice; officials of the side halls and rear chamber presented offerings separately.
translations.idiomatic: The Director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices presided at the sacrifice, while officials of the side halls and rear chamber presented offerings in turn.

sentences.zh: 六年，祠成，命曰「昭忠」，頒御書額，曰「表獎忠勛」。

translations.literal: In the sixth year the temple was completed; it was named "Manifest Loyalty," and an imperial inscription was bestowed reading "To Commend Loyal Merit."
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year the temple was completed and named the Temple of Manifest Loyalty; the court bestowed an imperial inscription reading "Commending Loyal Merit."

sentences.zh: 明年，循序定位，前殿正中祀敬謹庄親王尼堪，英誠武勛王揚古利，定南武壯王孔有德，贈忠勇王黃芳度，武襄公巴爾堪，凡五人。

translations.literal: The following year, positions were assigned in order. In the center of the front hall were enshrined Prince Jingjinzhuang Niken, Prince Yingchengwuxun Yangguli, Prince Dingnanwuzhuang Kong Youde, the posthumously enfeoffed Prince Zhongyong Huang Fangdu, and Duke Wuxiang Barkan—five men in all.
translations.idiomatic: The following year their positions were fixed in order. Enshrined in the center of the front hall were Prince Jingjinzhuang Niken, Prince Yingchengwuxun Yangguli, Prince Dingnanwuzhuang Kong Youde, the posthumously enfeoffed Prince Zhongyong Huang Fangdu, and Duke Wuxiang Barkan—five in all.

sentences.zh: 東次龕祀安北將軍佟國綱，一等公佟養正、達福、西哈，一等侯馬得功，一等伯巴什太，都統宜理布、巴都里，議政大臣程尼、穆和琳，大學士張泰，議政大臣羅沙，三等伯王之鼎，總督范承謨，額駙托柏，大學士龍西、色思泰，總督額倫特，尚書查弼納、圖捫，太子太保佟濟，倉場侍郎王秉仁，巡撫傅弘烈，都統博波圖，議政大臣雅賚、道禪、名蓋，參贊內大臣馬爾薩，凡二十八人。

translations.literal: In the eastern secondary niche were enshrined General Anbei Tong Guogang; the dukes of the first rank Tong Yangzheng, Dafu, and Xiha; the marquis of the first rank Ma Degong; the baron of the first rank Basitai; the commanders-in-chief Yilibu and Baduli; the Grand Ministers Cheng Ni and Mu Helin; Grand Secretary Zhang Tai; Grand Minister Luosha; the baron of the third rank Wang Zhiding; Governors-General Fan Chengmo and Elente; the imperial son-in-law Tuobai; Grand Secretaries Long Xi and Sise Tai; Ministers Chabina and Tumun; Grand Guardian of the Heir Apparent Tong Ji; Granary Commissioner Wang Bingren; Governor Fu Honglie; Commander-in-Chief Bobotu; Grand Ministers Yazai, Daoshan, and Minggai; and the Grand Minister Consultant Maersa—twenty-eight men in all.
translations.idiomatic: The eastern secondary niche enshrined General Anbei Tong Guogang; Dukes of the First Rank Tong Yangzheng, Dafu, and Xiha; Marquis of the First Rank Ma Degong; Baron of the First Rank Basitai; Commanders-in-Chief Yilibu and Baduli; Grand Ministers Cheng Ni and Mu Helin; Grand Secretary Zhang Tai; Grand Minister Luosha; Baron of the Third Rank Wang Zhiding; Governors-General Fan Chengmo and Elente; Imperial Son-in-Law Tuobai; Grand Secretaries Long Xi and Sise Tai; Ministers Chabina and Tumun; Grand Guardian of the Heir Apparent Tong Ji; Granary Commissioner Wang Bingren; Governor Fu Honglie; Commander-in-Chief Bobotu; Grand Ministers Yazai, Daoshan, and Minggai; and Grand Minister Consultant Maersa—twenty-eight in all.

sentences.zh: 西次龕祀續順公沈瑞，輔國公巴賽，大學士莫洛，尚書布顏岱，「十六大臣」綽和諾，巡撫柯永升，都統沙裡布，巡撫馬雄鎮，總督甘文焜、佟養甲，侍郎朝哈爾，鹽運使高天爵，參領費揚古，統領圖魯錫、喀爾他拉、喀爾護吉，副都統海蘭、蘇圖，統領胡裡布、哈克三，佐領葉喜，侍郎永國，統領阿爾岱，提督孫定遼，凡二十有四人。

translations.literal: In the western secondary niche were enshrined Duke Xushun Shen Rui; Duke Fuguo Basi; Grand Secretary Moluo; Minister Buyandai; Chuohenuo of the "Sixteen Grand Ministers"; Governors Ke Yongsheng and Ma Xiongzhen; Commander-in-Chief Shalibu; Governors-General Gan Wenkun and Tong Yangjia; Vice Minister Chaohaer; Salt Transport Commissioner Gao Tianjue; Company Commander Feiyanggu; commanders Tuluxi, Kaertala, and Kaerhuji; Vice Commanders-in-Chief Hailan and Sutu; commanders Hulibu and Hakesan; Assistant Commander Yexi; Vice Minister Yongguo; Commander Aerdai; and Provincial Military Commander Sun Dingliao—twenty-four men in all.
translations.idiomatic: The western secondary niche enshrined Duke Xushun Shen Rui, Duke Fuguo Basi, Grand Secretary Moluo, Minister Buyandai, Chuohenuo of the "Sixteen Grand Ministers," Governors Ke Yongsheng and Ma Xiongzhen, Commander-in-Chief Shalibu, Governors-General Gan Wenkun and Tong Yangjia, Vice Minister Chaohaer, Salt Transport Commissioner Gao Tianjue, Company Commander Feiyanggu, commanders Tuluxi, Kaertala, and Kaerhuji, Vice Commanders-in-Chief Hailan and Sutu, commanders Hulibu and Hakesan, Assistant Commander Yexi, Vice Minister Yongguo, Commander Aerdai, and Provincial Military Commander Sun Dingliao—twenty-four in all.

sentences.zh: 東又次龕統領劉哈，副都統盧錫、科布蘇、阿喀倪、納爾特、錫密賚、科爾坤、多頗洛、戴豪、渾錦、魏正、羅濟、阿什圖、覺羅阿克善、常祿、阿爾護、吉三、巴雅思虎朗，凡十有八人。

translations.literal: In the eastern tertiary niche were enshrined the commander Liu Ha; Vice Commanders-in-Chief Luxi, Kebusu, Akeni, Naerte, Ximibai, Keerkun, Duopoluo, Daihao, Hunjin, Weizheng, Luoji, Ashitu, the Aisin Gioro Akeshan, Changlu, Arhu, Jisan, and Bayasihulang—eighteen men in all.
translations.idiomatic: The eastern tertiary niche enshrined Commander Liu Ha and Vice Commanders-in-Chief Luxi, Kebusu, Akeni, Naerte, Ximibai, Keerkun, Duopoluo, Daihao, Hunjin, Weizheng, Luoji, Ashitu, the Aisin Gioro Akeshan, Changlu, Arhu, Jisan, and Bayasihulang—eighteen in all.

sentences.zh: 西又次龕提督段應舉，副都統穆舒、孟魁、白，原任巡撫賈維鑰，副都統邁圖，參領葛思特，巡撫硃國治、張文衡，侍郎馬如璧，糧道葉映榴，巡道陳啟泰，通政使莫洛渾，一等子穆克覃阿、納達、代音布，巡道陳丹赤，一等子覺羅莫洛渾，數亦如之。

translations.literal: In the western tertiary niche were enshrined Provincial Military Commander Duan Yingju; Vice Commanders-in-Chief Mushu, Mengkui, and Bai; the former Governor Jia Weiyao; Vice Commander-in-Chief Maitu; Company Commander Gesite; Governors Zhu Guozhi and Zhang Wenheng; Vice Minister Ma Rubi; Grain Intendant Ye Yingliu; Circuit Intendants Chen Qitai and Chen Danchi; Commissioner of the Office of Transmission Moluohun; Viscounts of the First Rank Mukedzanga, Nada, and Daiyinbu; and the Aisin Gioro Moluohun—the number was likewise.
translations.idiomatic: The western tertiary niche enshrined Provincial Military Commander Duan Yingju; Vice Commanders-in-Chief Mushu, Mengkui, and Bai; former Governor Jia Weiyao; Vice Commander-in-Chief Maitu; Company Commander Gesite; Governors Zhu Guozhi and Zhang Wenheng; Vice Minister Ma Rubi; Grain Intendant Ye Yingliu; Circuit Intendants Chen Qitai and Chen Danchi; Commissioner of the Office of Transmission Moluohun; Viscounts of the First Rank Mukedzanga, Nada, and Daiyinbu; and the Aisin Gioro Moluohun—the count was the same.

sentences.zh: 東末龕總兵吳萬福、徐勇、費雅達、硃天貴、張存福，都督僉事洪徵，總兵阿爾泰、歐陽凱，兵備道李懋祖，總兵楊佐，統領張廷輔，游擊楊光祖，統領定壽，總兵王承業，侍衛錫喇巴，布政使遲變龍，凡十有六人。

translations.literal: In the eastern rearmost niche were enshrined Regional Commanders Wu Wanfu, Xu Yong, Feiyada, Zhu Tiangui, and Zhang Cunfu; Regional Vice Commander Hong Zheng; Regional Commanders Aertai and Ouyang Kai; Military Intendant Li Maozu; Regional Commander Yang Zuo; commanders Zhang Tingfu and Dingshou; Brigadier Yang Guangzu; Regional Commander Wang Chengye; Bodyguard Xilaba; and Provincial Administration Commissioner Chi Bianlong—sixteen men in all.
translations.idiomatic: The eastern rearmost niche enshrined Regional Commanders Wu Wanfu, Xu Yong, Feiyada, Zhu Tiangui, and Zhang Cunfu; Regional Vice Commander Hong Zheng; Regional Commanders Aertai and Ouyang Kai; Military Intendant Li Maozu; Regional Commander Yang Zuo; commanders Zhang Tingfu and Dingshou; Brigadier Yang Guangzu; Regional Commander Wang Chengye; Bodyguard Xilaba; and Provincial Administration Commissioner Chi Bianlong—sixteen in all.

sentences.zh: 西末龕參領郭色，統領新泰，提督康泰，二等子覺羅顧納岱，總兵司九經，二等子拜蘭，總兵郝效忠、劉良臣，三等子巴郎、都爾莽鼐，副將楊虎，參將趙登舉，守備紀法，參將甘應龍，副將蔡隆，二等子拜三，一等男路什，總兵康海，凡十有七人。

translations.literal: In the western rearmost niche were enshrined Company Commander Guose; commander Xintai; Provincial Military Commander Kang Tai; the Aisin Gioro Viscount of the Second Rank Gunadai; Regional Commander Si Jiujing; Viscount of the Second Rank Bailan; Regional Commanders Hao Xiaozhong and Liu Liangchen; Viscounts of the Third Rank Balang and Duermangnai; Vice General Yang Hu; Assistant Generals Zhao Dengju and Gan Yinglong; Garrison Commander Ji Fa; Vice General Cai Long; Viscount of the Second Rank Baisan; Baron of the First Rank Lushi; and Regional Commander Kang Hai—seventeen men in all.
translations.idiomatic: The western rearmost niche enshrined Company Commander Guose, Commander Xintai, Provincial Military Commander Kang Tai, the Aisin Gioro Second-Rank Viscount Gunadai, Regional Commander Si Jiujing, Second-Rank Viscount Bailan, Regional Commanders Hao Xiaozhong and Liu Liangchen, Third-Rank Viscounts Balang and Duermangnai, Vice General Yang Hu, Assistant Generals Zhao Dengju and Gan Yinglong, Garrison Commander Ji Fa, Vice General Cai Long, Second-Rank Viscount Baisan, First-Rank Baron Lushi, and Regional Commander Kang Hai—seventeen in all.

sentences.zh: 後室、配樓、左右次龕、又次龕、兩廡暨各次龕，祀官千五百餘人。

translations.literal: In the rear chamber, side halls, left and right secondary niches, tertiary niches, both wings, and the various niches, more than fifteen hundred officials were enshrined.
translations.idiomatic: In the rear chamber, side halls, secondary and tertiary niches on either side, both wings, and the various subsidiary niches, more than fifteen hundred officials were enshrined.

sentences.zh: 東西房附祀兵士萬三百有奇。

translations.literal: In the eastern and western chambers soldiers enshrined in attendance numbered a little over ten thousand three hundred.
translations.idiomatic: In the eastern and western chambers, more than ten thousand three hundred soldiers were enshrined in subsidiary positions.

sentences.zh: 八年，定制以滿尚書、都統一人承祭，後室、兩廡，太常官分獻。

translations.literal: In the eighth year it was established by regulation that one Manchu Minister or Commander-in-Chief should preside over the sacrifice; for the rear chamber and both wings, officials of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices presented offerings separately.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year regulations fixed that one Manchu minister or commander-in-chief should preside at the sacrifice, while officials of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices presented offerings separately in the rear chamber and both wings.

sentences.zh: 十一年，令子孫居京秩者隨祭，

translations.literal: In the eleventh year it was ordered that descendants holding office in the capital should attend the sacrifice.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh year descendants who held office in the capital were required to attend the sacrifice.

sentences.zh: 乾隆十三年，諭祀陣亡總兵任舉、侍衛丹泰，旋令征金川陣沒將士併入之。

translations.literal: In the thirteenth year of Qianlong, an edict ordered the enshrinement of the fallen Regional Commander Ren Ju and Bodyguard Dantai; shortly thereafter officers and soldiers who died in battle during the Jinchuan campaign were also incorporated.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirteenth year of Qianlong, an edict directed that the fallen Regional Commander Ren Ju and Bodyguard Dantai be enshrined; shortly afterward officers and soldiers killed in the Jinchuan campaign were added as well.

sentences.zh: 十五年，祀都統傅清、左都御史拉布敦。

translations.literal: In the fifteenth year Commanders-in-Chief Fu Qing and Censor-in-Chief of the Left Labudun were enshrined.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifteenth year Commanders-in-Chief Fu Qing and Censor-in-Chief of the Left Labudun were added to the temple.

sentences.zh: 十八年，追封巴爾堪、巴賽並為簡親王。

translations.literal: In the eighteenth year Barkan and Basi were both posthumously enfeoffed as Princes Jian.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighteenth year Barkan and Basi were both posthumously enfeoffed as Princes Jian.

sentences.zh: 移巴爾堪位揚古利上，巴賽位孔有德上。

translations.literal: Barkan's position was moved above Yangguli's, and Basi's above Kong Youde's.
translations.idiomatic: Barkan's tablet was moved to a position above Yangguli's, and Basi's above Kong Youde's.

sentences.zh: 初，前室左右各三龕，止序爵秩，不系時代。

translations.literal: At first, on the left and right of the front chamber there were three niches each, ordered only by rank and title, without regard to period.
translations.idiomatic: Initially the front chamber had three niches on each side, arranged solely by rank and title, without regard to historical period.

sentences.zh: 至是定議，自天命以來，按代序官，同代同官序年月，依賢良祠例，按時班爵為序。

translations.literal: At this point it was decided that from the Tianming reign onward officials should be ordered by reign; within the same reign and the same office, they should be ordered by year and month; following the precedent of the Temple of Worthies, they should be arranged by the sequence of ranks at the time.
translations.idiomatic: It was then decided that from the Tianming era onward officials should be arranged by reign; within the same reign and rank, by year and month; following the precedent of the Temple of Worthies, by the order of their titles at the time.

sentences.zh: 其兵士設位，分前、後廡，以橫板隔別之。

translations.literal: Positions for soldiers were divided between the front and rear wings and separated by horizontal boards.
translations.idiomatic: Soldiers' positions were divided between the front and rear wings and separated by horizontal partitions.

sentences.zh: 中葉以後入祀者，將軍班第、明瑞、溫福，都統滿福、扎拉豐阿，參贊大臣鄂容安，統領觀音保、烏三太、台斐音阿，提督許世亨，副都統呼爾起阿、第木保、覺羅明善，總兵王玉廷、李全、德福、貴林、張朝龍，而海蘭察以病沒，端濟布以傷，亦併入之。

translations.literal: Those enshrined after the mid-dynasty included Generals Bandi, Mingrui, and Wenfu; Commanders-in-Chief Manfu and Zhalafeng'a; Grand Minister Consultant Erong'an; commanders Guanyinbao, Wusantai, and Taifei'ina; Provincial Military Commander Xu Shiheng; Vice Commanders-in-Chief Hu'erqi'a, Dimubao, and the Aisin Gioro Mingshan; and Regional Commanders Wang Yuting, Li Quan, Defu, Guilin, and Zhang Chaolong; Hailancha, who died of illness, and Duanjibu, who died of wounds, were also incorporated.
translations.idiomatic: Those enshrined in the mid-dynasty period included Generals Bandi, Mingrui, and Wenfu; Commanders-in-Chief Manfu and Zhalafeng'a; Grand Minister Consultant Erong'an; commanders Guanyinbao, Wusantai, and Taifei'ina; Provincial Military Commander Xu Shiheng; Vice Commanders-in-Chief Hu'erqi'a, Dimubao, and the Aisin Gioro Mingshan; and Regional Commanders Wang Yuting, Li Quan, Defu, Guilin, and Zhang Chaolong; Hailancha, who died of illness, and Duanjibu, who died of wounds, were added as well.

sentences.zh: 至典史溫模死守通渭，從容就義，特予入祠。

translations.literal: As for the district clerk Wen Mo, who defended Tongwei to the death and met his end with composure, he was specially granted enshrinement.
translations.idiomatic: The district clerk Wen Mo, who held Tongwei to the death and met his end with composure, was specially granted a place in the temple.

sentences.zh: 且有取義捨生，賞延於世，褒諭流外微官，獲邀䘏廕，茂典也。

translations.literal: Moreover, because he chose righteousness and abandoned life, his reward extended to posterity; an edict of praise was issued to this minor official from beyond the regular stream, who received the grant of posthumous enfeoffment—a splendid precedent.
translations.idiomatic: Because he chose righteousness over life, his reward extended to his descendants; the court issued a commendation for this low-ranking official from outside the regular bureaucracy, granting posthumous honors—a splendid precedent indeed.

sentences.zh: 嘉慶朝，祀大學士福康安、將軍德楞泰、提督花連布、總兵多爾濟札普、知縣強克捷。

translations.literal: In the Jiaqing reign were enshrined Grand Secretary Fukang'an, General Delin Tai, Provincial Military Commander Hualianbu, Regional Commander Duo'erjizhake, and District Magistrate Qiang Kejie.
translations.idiomatic: During the Jiaqing reign the temple received Grand Secretary Fukang'an, General Delin Tai, Provincial Military Commander Hualianbu, Regional Commander Duo'erjizhake, and District Magistrate Qiang Kejie.

sentences.zh: 先是，康熙間，巡撫曹申吉已入祠，至是以阿附吳三桂按實，奪之。

translations.literal: Earlier, during the Kangxi reign, Governor Cao Shenji had already been enshrined; at this point, because he had attached himself to Wu Sangui, upon investigation the fact was established and his enshrinement was revoked.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, during the Kangxi reign, Governor Cao Shenji had been enshrined; now, having been found to have sided with Wu Sangui, his place in the temple was revoked.

sentences.zh: 時各省言沒王事者，奏報猥雜，龕位不給，於是詔建各省昭忠祠。

translations.literal: At the time memorials from the provinces concerning those who died in service to the ruler were numerous and disorderly, and niche positions were insufficient; therefore an edict ordered the establishment of Temples of Manifest Loyalty in each province.
translations.idiomatic: Memorials from the provinces reporting officials who had died in the ruler's service had become so numerous and disorderly that niche space in the capital temple was exhausted; the court therefore ordered Temples of Manifest Loyalty to be built in each province.

sentences.zh: 其京祠定文三品、武二品以上，及八旗官弁為限，已祀者如故。

translations.literal: For the capital temple the limit was set at civil officials of the third rank and above, military officials of the second rank and above, and Banner officers; those already enshrined remained as before.
translations.idiomatic: The capital temple was limited to civil officials of the third rank and above, military officials of the second rank and above, and Banner officers; those already enshrined were not affected.

sentences.zh: 嗣是卑官預祀，視特旨行。

translations.literal: Thereafter, whether low-ranking officials might be enshrined depended on special imperial order.
translations.idiomatic: Thereafter, enshrinement of lower-ranking officials required a special imperial directive.

sentences.zh: 故事，承祭官循例朝服，今改蟒袍補服，示別壇廟也。

translations.literal: By precedent the presiding official wore court dress according to regulation; now it was changed to python robe with rank badge, to distinguish this altar from other temples.
translations.idiomatic: By precedent the presiding official wore standard court dress; this was changed to python robe with rank badge to distinguish this altar from other temples.

sentences.zh: 道光初元，以國初殉難副將楊祖光等入祀，厥後賡入者，都統巴彥巴圖、烏凌阿、印登額，參贊大臣慶祥，總督裕謙，提督海凌阿、關天培、陳化成，副都統海齡、長喜，總兵萬建功、祥福、葛雲飛、鄭國鴻、王錫朋、謝朝恩、江繼芸、慶和、吳喜，副將烏大魁、馬韜、周承恩、劉大忠、陳連升、硃貴、瑪隆阿、伊克坦布等。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Daoguang reign the Vice General Yang Zuguang and others who had died in the calamity at the founding of the state were enshrined; those subsequently added in succession included Commanders-in-Chief Bayanbatu, Wuling'a, and Yindeng'e; Grand Minister Consultant Qingxiang; Governor-General Yu Qian; Provincial Military Commanders Hailing'a, Guan Tianpei, and Chen Huacheng; Vice Commanders-in-Chief Hailing and Changxi; Regional Commanders Wan Jiangong, Xiangfu, Ge Yunfei, Zheng Guohong, Wang Xipeng, Xie Chao'en, Jiang Jiyun, Qinghe, and Wu Xi; and Vice Generals Wudakui, Ma Tao, Zhou Chengen, Liu Dazhong, Chen Liansheng, Zhu Gui, Malong'a, Yiketanbu, and others.
translations.idiomatic: At the opening of the Daoguang reign Vice General Yang Zuguang and others who had died defending the dynasty in its early years were enshrined; those added later included Commanders-in-Chief Bayanbatu, Wuling'a, and Yindeng'e, Grand Minister Consultant Qingxiang, Governor-General Yu Qian, Provincial Military Commanders Hailing'a, Guan Tianpei, and Chen Huacheng, Vice Commanders-in-Chief Hailing and Changxi, Regional Commanders Wan Jiangong, Xiangfu, Ge Yunfei, Zheng Guohong, Wang Xipeng, Xie Chao'en, Jiang Jiyun, Qinghe, and Wu Xi, and Vice Generals Wudakui, Ma Tao, Zhou Chengen, Liu Dazhong, Chen Liansheng, Zhu Gui, Malong'a, Yiketanbu, and others.

sentences.zh: 其卑秩中，如知縣楊延亮、縣丞方振聲、守備馬步衢、把總陳玉威，亦足多者。

translations.literal: Among those of low rank, such as District Magistrate Yang Yanliang, Assistant Magistrate Fang Zhensheng, Garrison Commander Ma Buqi, and Platoon Commander Chen Yuwei, there were also many worthy of praise.
translations.idiomatic: Among the lower ranks as well—District Magistrate Yang Yanliang, Assistant Magistrate Fang Zhensheng, Garrison Commander Ma Buqi, and Platoon Commander Chen Yuwei—there were many equally deserving of honor.

sentences.zh: 雍正初，各省立忠義祠，凡已旌表者，設位祠中，春、秋展祀。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Yongzheng reign, Temples of Loyalty and Righteousness were established in each province; all who had received commendation were given positions in the temples, with sacrifices in spring and autumn.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Yongzheng reign each province established Temples of Loyalty and Righteousness; all who had received official commendation were given places in the temples and honored with spring and autumn sacrifices.

sentences.zh: 乾隆四十一年，定明代殉國諸臣，既邀諡典，並許入祠。

translations.literal: In the forty-first year of Qianlong it was fixed that Ming officials who had died for the state, having already received posthumous titles, should also be permitted enshrinement.
translations.idiomatic: In the forty-first year of the Qianlong reign it was decided that Ming officials who had died for their country, having already received posthumous titles, should also be permitted enshrinement.

sentences.zh: 又諸生、韋布、山樵、市隱者流，遂志成仁，亦如前例。

translations.literal: Moreover, licentiates, commoners in hemp cloth, woodcutters in the hills, and recluses in the marketplace who fulfilled their resolve and achieved humanity were treated according to the same precedent.
translations.idiomatic: Licentiates, commoners, hill woodcutters, and marketplace recluses who fulfilled their resolve and died for their principles were likewise treated under the same precedent.

sentences.zh: 嘉慶七年，始令各省府城建昭忠祠，或附祀關帝及城隍廟，凡陣亡文武官暨兵士、鄉勇，按籍入祀。

translations.literal: In the seventh year of Jiaqing it was first ordered that each provincial capital should build a Temple of Manifest Loyalty, or attach the worship to temples of Lord Guan or the City God; all civil and military officials, soldiers, and local militia who died in battle were to be enshrined according to register.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year of Jiaqing each provincial capital was ordered to build a Temple of Manifest Loyalty, or to attach the rites to temples of Lord Guan or the City God; all civil and military officials, soldiers, and local militia killed in battle were to be enshrined according to the rolls.

sentences.zh: 八旗二品以上官已祀京祠者，仍許陣亡所在地祠祀，合五十人一龕，位祀正中，兵勇則百人或數十人一位，分列兩旁，駐防位綠營上。

translations.literal: Banner officials of the second rank and above already enshrined in the capital temple were still permitted enshrinement in the temple at the place where they fell; fifty men shared one niche, with the position in the center; for soldiers and militia, one position was shared by a hundred or several dozen men, arranged on either side; garrison troops were placed above Green Standard troops.
translations.idiomatic: Banner officials of the second rank and above already enshrined in the capital might still be honored in the provincial temple where they fell: fifty men per niche, centered in the shrine; soldiers and militia shared positions of a hundred or several dozen each, arranged on either side, with garrison troops placed above Green Standard troops.

sentences.zh: 春、秋二奠，有司親蒞，用少牢，果品、上香、薦帛、三獻如儀。

translations.literal: In the spring and autumn offerings local officials attended in person; the lesser tai lao was used, with fruit, incense, presentation of silk, and three offerings according to ritual.
translations.idiomatic: For the spring and autumn sacrifices local officials attended in person, using the lesser tai lao offering, with fruit, incense, silk presentation, and three libations performed according to ritual.

sentences.zh: 同治二年，允曾國籓請，江寧建昭忠祠，祀湖南水陸師陣亡員弁。

translations.literal: In the second year of Tongzhi, upon Zeng Guofan's request, a Temple of Manifest Loyalty was built at Jiangning to enshrine the officers of the Hunan land and naval forces who had died in battle.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Tongzhi, at Zeng Guofan's request, a Temple of Manifest Loyalty was built at Jiangning to honor officers of the Hunan land and naval forces killed in battle.

sentences.zh: 已復抗節官紳亦許崇祀，並建專祠。

translations.literal: Officials and gentry who had upheld integrity were also permitted honored enshrinement, and dedicated temples were also built.
translations.idiomatic: Officials and local gentry who had upheld their integrity were also permitted honored enshrinement, and dedicated temples were built for them as well.

sentences.zh: 婦女殉難者，亦別立貞烈祠雲。

translations.literal: Women who died in the calamity also had separate Temples of Chaste Martyrs established.
translations.idiomatic: Women who died in the line of duty were likewise honored in separate Temples of Chaste Martyrs.

sentences.zh: 賢良祠雍正八年詔曰：「古者大烝之祭，凡法施於民，以勞定國者，皆列祀典，受明禋。

translations.literal: Temple of Worthies. In the eighth year of Yongzheng an edict stated: "In antiquity, at the great seasonal offering, all whose laws benefited the people and whose labor settled the state were entered in the sacrificial canon and received bright offerings.
translations.idiomatic: The Temple of Worthies. In the eighth year of Yongzheng an edict declared: "In antiquity, at the great seasonal sacrifice, all whose laws benefited the people and whose labor secured the state were entered in the sacrificial canon and received bright offerings.

sentences.zh: 我朝開國以後，名臣碩輔，先後相望。

translations.literal: Since the founding of our dynasty, eminent ministers and great assistants have succeeded one another without interruption.
translations.idiomatic: Since our dynasty was founded, eminent ministers and great statesmen have succeeded one another in an unbroken line.

sentences.zh: 或勛垂節鉞，或節厲冰霜，既樹羽儀，宜隆俎豆。

translations.literal: Some have left their merit in military seals and axes; others have made their integrity stern as frost and ice; having already raised the ceremonial insignia, they should be exalted with sacrificial vessels.
translations.idiomatic: Some left their merit on the battlefield; others held their integrity firm as frost and ice; having already served as models of statesmanship, they deserve the highest sacrificial honors.

sentences.zh: 俾世世為臣者，觀感奮發，知所慕效。

translations.literal: So that subjects in every generation, beholding and being moved, may be stirred to exertion and know whom to emulate.
translations.idiomatic: So that officials in every generation, moved by their example, may be stirred to worthy service and know whom to emulate.

sentences.zh: 庶明良喜起，副予厚期。

translations.literal: Thus may ruler and minister rejoice together and rise, fulfilling my deep expectations.
translations.idiomatic: Thus may ruler and minister flourish together in mutual trust, fulfilling my deepest hopes.

sentences.zh: 京師宜擇地建祠，命曰『賢良』，春、秋展祀，永光盛典。」

translations.literal: In the capital a site should be chosen to build a temple, named "Worthy," with sacrifices in spring and autumn, that this splendid ceremony may shine forever."
translations.idiomatic: A site should be chosen in the capital to build a temple named the Temple of Worthies, with sacrifices in spring and autumn, so that this splendid rite may endure forever."

sentences.zh: 乃營廟宇在地安門外西偏，正殿、後室各五楹，東、西廡，歲春、秋仲月，諏吉，遣官致祭。

translations.literal: Thereupon a temple was built on the western side outside Di'an Gate; the main hall and rear chamber each had five bays, with eastern and western wings; each year in the second month of spring and autumn an auspicious day was chosen and an official was dispatched to perform the sacrifice.
translations.idiomatic: Accordingly a temple was erected on the western side outside Di'an Gate, with five bays each in the main hall and rear chamber and eastern and western wings; each year in the second month of spring and of autumn an auspicious day was chosen and an official was sent to conduct the sacrifice.

sentences.zh: 前殿案各素帛一、羊一、豕一、果五盤。

translations.literal: On each table in the front hall were one piece of plain silk, one sheep, one pig, and five trays of fruit.
translations.idiomatic: Each table in the front hall bore one piece of plain silk, one sheep, one pig, and five trays of fruit.

sentences.zh: 後室果品同，唯牲、帛共案而具一。

translations.literal: In the rear chamber the fruit was the same, but the sacrificial animals and silk were shared on one table with only one set.
translations.idiomatic: The rear chamber had the same fruit offerings, but the sacrificial animals and silk were shared on a single table with one set only.

sentences.zh: 承祭官蟒服，二跪六叩三獻。

translations.literal: The presiding official wore a python robe; he knelt twice, kowtowed six times, and presented three offerings.
translations.idiomatic: The presiding official wore a python robe, knelt twice, kowtowed six times, and presented three libations.

sentences.zh: 餘如常儀。

translations.literal: The remainder followed the usual ritual.
translations.idiomatic: All other rites followed the usual procedure.

sentences.zh: 於是僉議怡賢親王允祥，宗功元祀，宜居首。

translations.literal: Thereupon all agreed that Prince Yixian Yunxiang, whose clan merit was the primal sacrifice, should occupy the foremost position.
translations.idiomatic: All agreed that Prince Yixian Yunxiang, whose service to the imperial clan was foundational, should occupy the foremost position.

sentences.zh: 大學士、公圖海，公賴塔，大學士張英，尚書顧八代、馬爾漢、趙申喬，河道總督靳輔、齊蘇勒，總督楊宗仁，巡撫陳璸，咸列其選。

translations.literal: Grand Secretary and Duke Tu Hai, Duke Laita, Grand Secretary Zhang Ying, Ministers Gu Badai, Ma Erhan, and Zhao Shenqiao, Directors-General of Rivers Jin Fu and Qisuole, Governor-General Yang Zongren, and Governor Chen Bin were all listed among the selections.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Secretary and Duke Tu Hai, Duke Laita, Grand Secretary Zhang Ying, Ministers Gu Badai, Ma Erhan, and Zhao Shenqiao, Directors-General of Rivers Jin Fu and Qisuole, Governor-General Yang Zongren, and Governor Chen Bin were all chosen for enshrinement.

sentences.zh: 自是先後賡續入祠者，大學士范文程、巴克什達海、阿蘭泰、李之芳、吳琠、張玉書、李光地、富寧安、張鵬翮、寧完我、魏裔介、額色黑、王熙，領侍衛內大臣福善、費揚古、尹德，尚書勵杜訥、徐潮、姚文然、魏象樞、湯斌，提督張勇、王進寶、孫思克、施琅，總督趙良棟、于成龍、傅臘塔、孟喬芳、李國英，都統馮國相、李國翰、根特，統領莽依圖，將軍阿爾納、愛星阿、佛尼埒，副都統褚庫巴圖魯。

translations.literal: From this time those subsequently added to the temple in succession included Grand Secretaries Fan Wencheng, Bakshi Dahai, Alantai, Li Zhifang, Wu Qi, Zhang Yushu, Li Guangdi, Funing'an, Zhang Penghe, Ning Wanwo, Wei Yijie, Esehei, and Wang Xi; Chief Grand Ministers Fushan, Feiyanggu, and Yinde; Ministers Li Dun'e, Xu Chao, Yao Wenran, Wei Xiangju, and Tang Bin; Provincial Military Commanders Zhang Yong, Wang Jinbao, Sun Sike, and Shi Lang; Governors-General Zhao Liangdong, Yu Chenglong, Fulata, Meng Qiaofang, and Li Guoying; Commanders-in-Chief Feng Guoxiang, Li Guohan, and Gent; commander Mangyitu; Generals A'erna, Aixing'a, and Fonilie; and Vice Commander-in-Chief Chukubaturu.
translations.idiomatic: Thereafter those added in succession included Grand Secretaries Fan Wencheng, Bakshi Dahai, Alantai, Li Zhifang, Wu Qi, Zhang Yushu, Li Guangdi, Funing'an, Zhang Penghe, Ning Wanwo, Wei Yijie, Esehei, and Wang Xi; Chief Grand Ministers Fushan, Feiyanggu, and Yinde; Ministers Li Dun'e, Xu Chao, Yao Wenran, Wei Xiangju, and Tang Bin; Provincial Military Commanders Zhang Yong, Wang Jinbao, Sun Sike, and Shi Lang; Governors-General Zhao Liangdong, Yu Chenglong, Fulata, Meng Qiaofang, and Li Guoying; Commanders-in-Chief Feng Guoxiang, Li Guohan, and Gent; Commander Mangyitu; Generals A'erna, Aixing'a, and Fonilie; and Vice Commander-in-Chief Chukubaturu.

sentences.zh: 明年祠成，頒御書額曰「崇忠念舊」，設位為祭。

translations.literal: The following year the temple was completed; an imperial inscription was bestowed reading "Honoring Loyalty and Cherishing the Past," and positions were set for sacrifice.
translations.idiomatic: The following year the temple was completed; the court bestowed an imperial inscription reading "Honoring Loyalty and Cherishing the Past," and tablets were installed for worship.

sentences.zh: 前殿內大臣或散秩大臣、尚書、都統主之。

translations.literal: The front hall was presided over by a Grand Minister of the Imperial Bodyguard, or a Minister without regular rank, a Minister, or a Commander-in-Chief.
translations.idiomatic: The front hall sacrifice was presided over by a Grand Minister of the Imperial Bodyguard, a Minister without regular rank, a Minister, or a Commander-in-Chief.

sentences.zh: 後殿用太常寺長官。

translations.literal: The rear hall used the chief official of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices.
translations.idiomatic: The rear hall sacrifice was conducted by the chief official of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices.

sentences.zh: 入祠日，子孫咸與行禮，春、秋遣官陪祀同。

translations.literal: On the day of enshrinement all descendants participated in the rites; in spring and autumn dispatched officials assisted in the sacrifice in the same manner.
translations.idiomatic: On the day of enshrinement all descendants took part in the rites; in spring and autumn dispatched officials assisted at the sacrifice in the same way.

sentences.zh: 十二年，祀大學士田從典、高其位。

translations.literal: In the twelfth year Grand Secretaries Tian Congdian and Gao Qiwei were enshrined.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth year Grand Secretaries Tian Congdian and Gao Qiwei were added to the temple.

sentences.zh: 乾隆元年，命入祀諸臣未予諡者悉追予。

translations.literal: In the first year of Qianlong it was ordered that all officials enshrined who had not received posthumous titles should be granted them retroactively.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Qianlong all enshrined officials who had not received posthumous titles were granted them retroactively.

sentences.zh: 是歲祀尚書銜兼祭酒楊名時，大學士硃軾，內大臣哈世屯，尚書米思翰。

translations.literal: That year were enshrined Yang Mingshi, Minister by title and concurrent Chancellor of the National University; Grand Secretary Zhu Shi; Grand Minister Hashitun; and Minister Misihan.
translations.idiomatic: That year the temple received Yang Mingshi, Minister by title and concurrent Chancellor of the National University, Grand Secretary Zhu Shi, Grand Minister Hashitun, and Minister Misihan.

sentences.zh: 五年，祀總督李衛。

translations.literal: In the fifth year Governor-General Li Wei was enshrined.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year Governor-General Li Wei was added to the temple.

sentences.zh: 明年，祀尚書徐元夢，巡撫徐士林。

translations.literal: The following year Minister Xu Yuanmeng and Governor Xu Shilin were enshrined.
translations.idiomatic: The following year Minister Xu Yuanmeng and Governor Xu Shilin were added to the temple.

sentences.zh: 十年，釐定祠位，前殿正中祀怡賢親王，後室諸臣合一龕。

translations.literal: In the tenth year temple positions were fixed: in the center of the front hall Prince Yixian was enshrined; in the rear chamber all the officials were combined in one niche.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth year the arrangement of tablets was fixed: Prince Yixian occupied the center of the front hall, while all other officials in the rear chamber shared a single niche.

sentences.zh: 首世次最先者，餘分左右行，按世序爵，大學士居前，次領侍衛內大臣、尚書、都統、將軍、總督、前鋒護軍統領、提督、侍郎、巡撫、副都統，以次分列。

translations.literal: The one of the earliest generation came first; the rest were divided into left and right rows, ordered by generation and rank: Grand Secretaries came first, then Chief Grand Ministers of the Imperial Bodyguard, Ministers, Commanders-in-Chief, Generals, Governors-General, commanders of the Vanguard and Guard, Provincial Military Commanders, Vice Ministers, Governors, and Vice Commanders-in-Chief, each class arranged in order.
translations.idiomatic: The earliest generation came first; the rest were arranged in left and right rows by generation and rank—Grand Secretaries first, then Chief Grand Ministers, Ministers, Commanders-in-Chief, Generals, Governors-General, Vanguard and Guard commanders, Provincial Military Commanders, Vice Ministers, Governors, and Vice Commanders-in-Chief, each rank in its proper order.

sentences.zh: 至世爵有子、男授尚書、都統者，有侯、伯為侍郎、副都統者，仍視官秩為差。

translations.literal: As for hereditary nobles, when viscounts and barons were appointed Ministers or Commanders-in-Chief, or marquises and earls served as Vice Ministers or Vice Commanders-in-Chief, they were still ranked according to their official posts.
translations.idiomatic: When hereditary nobles held concurrent offices—viscounts and barons as Ministers or Commanders-in-Chief, marquises and earls as Vice Ministers or Vice Commanders-in-Chief—they were still ranked according to their official posts.

sentences.zh: 嗣是入祀，則超勇親王策凌，列怡賢親王左次龕。

translations.literal: Thereafter those enshrined included Prince Chaoyong Celeng, placed in the secondary niche to the left of Prince Yixian.
translations.idiomatic: Those added later included Prince Chaoyong Celeng, placed in the secondary niche to the left of Prince Yixian.

sentences.zh: 名臣則大學士馬齊、伊桑阿、福敏、黃廷桂、蔣溥、史貽直、梁詩正、來保、傅恆、尹繼善、陳宏謀、劉綸、劉統勛、舒赫德、高晉、英廉、徐本、高斌，協辦大學士兆惠，左都御史拉布敦，尚書汪由敦、李元亮、阿里袞，尚書銜錢陳群，都統傅清，將軍和起、伊勒圖、奎林，總督那蘇圖、陳大受、喀爾吉善、鶴年、吳達善、何煟、袁守侗、方觀承、薩載、提督許世亨，巡撫潘思榘、鄂弼、李湖、傅弘烈。

translations.literal: Among eminent ministers were Grand Secretaries Ma Qi, Yisang'a, Fumin, Huang Tinggui, Jiang Pu, Shi Yizhi, Liang Shizheng, Laibao, Fu Heng, Yin Jishan, Chen Hongmou, Liu Lun, Liu Tongxun, Suhede, Gao Jin, Yinglian, Xu Ben, and Gao Bin; Associate Grand Secretary Zhaohui; Censor-in-Chief of the Left Labudun; Ministers Wang Youdun, Li Yuanliang, and Aligun; Qian Chenqun by Minister's title; Commander-in-Chief Fu Qing; Generals Heqi, Yiletu, and Kuilin; Governors-General Nasutu, Chen Dashou, Ka'erjishan, Henian, Wu Dashan, He Wei, Yuan Shoutong, Fang Guancheng, and Sazai; Provincial Military Commander Xu Shiheng; and Governors Pan Sirong, Ebi, Li Hu, and Fu Honglie.
translations.idiomatic: Among eminent ministers enshrined were Grand Secretaries Ma Qi, Yisang'a, Fumin, Huang Tinggui, Jiang Pu, Shi Yizhi, Liang Shizheng, Laibao, Fu Heng, Yin Jishan, Chen Hongmou, Liu Lun, Liu Tongxun, Suhede, Gao Jin, Yinglian, Xu Ben, and Gao Bin; Associate Grand Secretary Zhaohui; Censor-in-Chief of the Left Labudun; Ministers Wang Youdun, Li Yuanliang, and Aligun; Qian Chenqun by Minister's title; Commander-in-Chief Fu Qing; Generals Heqi, Yiletu, and Kuilin; Governors-General Nasutu, Chen Dashou, Ka'erjishan, Henian, Wu Dashan, He Wei, Yuan Shoutong, Fang Guancheng, and Sazai; Provincial Military Commander Xu Shiheng; and Governors Pan Sirong, Ebi, Li Hu, and Fu Honglie.

sentences.zh: 弘烈自雍正時，拉布敦、傅清自乾隆時，併入昭忠祠，今再祀賢良者也。

translations.literal: Honglie from the Yongzheng reign, and Labudun and Fu Qing from the Qianlong reign, had been incorporated into the Temple of Manifest Loyalty; now they were again enshrined in the Temple of Worthies.
translations.idiomatic: Fu Honglie had been enshrined in the Temple of Manifest Loyalty since the Yongzheng reign, and Labudun and Fu Qing since Qianlong; now they were honored again in the Temple of Worthies.

sentences.zh: 嘉慶朝，則祀大學士福康安、阿桂、劉墉、王傑、硃珪、戴衢亨、董誥，尚書董邦達、彭元瑞、奉寬，總督鄂輝。

translations.literal: In the Jiaqing reign were enshrined Grand Secretaries Fukang'an, Agui, Liu Yong, Wang Jie, Zhu Gui, Dai Quheng, and Dong Gao; Ministers Dong Bangda, Peng Yuanrui, and Feng Kuan; and Governor-General E Hui.
translations.idiomatic: During the Jiaqing reign the temple received Grand Secretaries Fukang'an, Agui, Liu Yong, Wang Jie, Zhu Gui, Dai Quheng, and Dong Gao; Ministers Dong Bangda, Peng Yuanrui, and Feng Kuan; and Governor-General E Hui.

sentences.zh: 道光朝，則祀大學士富俊、曹振鏞、托津、長齡、盧廕溥、文孚、王鼎，協辦大學士汪廷珍、陳官俊，尚書黃鉞、隆文，將軍玉麟，總督楊遇春、陶澍，河道總督黎世序。

translations.literal: In the Daoguang reign were enshrined Grand Secretaries Fujun, Cao Zhenyong, Tuojin, Changling, Lu Yinpu, Wen Fu, and Wang Ding; Associate Grand Secretaries Wang Tingzhen and Chen Guanjun; Ministers Huang Yue and Long Wen; General Yulin; Governors-General Yang Yuchun and Tao Shu; and Director-General of Rivers Li Shixu.
translations.idiomatic: During the Daoguang reign the temple received Grand Secretaries Fujun, Cao Zhenyong, Tuojin, Changling, Lu Yinpu, Wen Fu, and Wang Ding; Associate Grand Secretaries Wang Tingzhen and Chen Guanjun; Ministers Huang Yue and Long Wen; General Yulin; Governors-General Yang Yuchun and Tao Shu; and Director-General of Rivers Li Shixu.

sentences.zh: 咸豐朝，則祀大學士潘世恩、文慶、裕誠，協辦大學士杜受田，侍郎杜堮，巡撫胡林翼。

translations.literal: In the Xianfeng reign were enshrined Grand Secretaries Pan Shien, Wen Qing, and Yu Cheng; Associate Grand Secretary Du Shoutian; Vice Minister Du E; and Governor Hu Linyi.
translations.idiomatic: During the Xianfeng reign the temple received Grand Secretaries Pan Shien, Wen Qing, and Yu Cheng; Associate Grand Secretary Du Shoutian; Vice Minister Du E; and Governor Hu Linyi.

sentences.zh: 同治朝，則祀大學士桂良、祁俊藻、官文、倭仁、曾國籓、瑞常、賈楨，大學士銜翁心存，協辦大學士駱秉章，總督沈兆霖、馬新貽。

translations.literal: In the Tongzhi reign were enshrined Grand Secretaries Gui Liang, Qi Junzao, Guan Wen, Woren, Zeng Guofan, Ruichang, and Jia Zhen; Weng Xincun by Grand Secretary's title; Associate Grand Secretary Luo Bingzhang; and Governors-General Shen Zhaolin and Ma Xinyi.
translations.idiomatic: During the Tongzhi reign the temple received Grand Secretaries Gui Liang, Qi Junzao, Guan Wen, Woren, Zeng Guofan, Ruichang, and Jia Zhen; Weng Xincun by Grand Secretary's title; Associate Grand Secretary Luo Bingzhang; and Governors-General Shen Zhaolin and Ma Xinyi.

sentences.zh: 其光緒朝入祀者，恭忠親王奕訢。

translations.literal: Those enshrined in the Guangxu reign included Prince Gongzhong Yixin.
translations.idiomatic: Those enshrined during the Guangxu reign included Prince Gongzhong Yixin.

sentences.zh: 名臣大學士文祥、英桂、全慶、載齡、左宗棠、靈桂、寶鋆、恩承、福錕、張之萬、麟書、額勒和布、李鴻章、榮祿、裕德、昆岡、崇禮、敬信，協辦大學士沈桂芬、李鴻藻，將軍長順，總督沈葆楨、丁寶楨、岑毓英、曾國荃、劉坤一，提督宋慶，巡撫張曜也。

translations.literal: Among eminent ministers were Grand Secretaries Wen Xiang, Yinggui, Quanqing, Zailing, Zuo Zongtang, Linggui, Baojun, Encheng, Fukun, Zhang Zhiwan, Linshu, Elehebu, Li Hongzhang, Ronglu, Yude, Kungang, Chongli, and Jingxin; Associate Grand Secretaries Shen Guifen and Li Hongzao; General Changshun; Governors-General Shen Baozhen, Ding Baozhen, Cen Yuying, Zeng Guoquan, and Liu Kunyi; Provincial Military Commander Song Qing; and Governor Zhang Yao.
translations.idiomatic: Among eminent ministers were Grand Secretaries Wen Xiang, Yinggui, Quanqing, Zailing, Zuo Zongtang, Linggui, Baojun, Encheng, Fukun, Zhang Zhiwan, Linshu, Elehebu, Li Hongzhang, Ronglu, Yude, Kungang, Chongli, and Jingxin; Associate Grand Secretaries Shen Guifen and Li Hongzao; General Changshun; Governors-General Shen Baozhen, Ding Baozhen, Cen Yuying, Zeng Guoquan, and Liu Kunyi; Provincial Military Commander Song Qing; and Governor Zhang Yao.

sentences.zh: 宣統初入祀者，止大學士王文韶、張之洞、孫家鼐、鹿傳霖，協辦大學士戴鴻慈五人而已。

translations.literal: Those enshrined at the beginning of Xuantong were only five: Grand Secretaries Wang Wenshao, Zhang Zhidong, Sun Jianai, and Lu Chuanlin, and Associate Grand Secretary Dai Hongci.
translations.idiomatic: Those enshrined at the beginning of the Xuantong reign were only five in all: Grand Secretaries Wang Wenshao, Zhang Zhidong, Sun Jianai, and Lu Chuanlin, and Associate Grand Secretary Dai Hongci.

sentences.zh: 各省賢良祠，雍正十年，詔：「各省會地建祠宇，凡外任文武大臣，忠勇威愛，公論允翕者，俾膺祀典，用勸在官。

translations.literal: Provincial Temples of Worthies. In the tenth year of Yongzheng an edict stated: "In each provincial capital a temple shall be built; all civil and military great ministers serving outside the capital who are loyal, brave, awe-inspiring, and loving, and whom public opinion unanimously approves, shall receive the sacrificial canon, to encourage those in office.
translations.idiomatic: Provincial Temples of Worthies. In the tenth year of Yongzheng an edict declared: "A temple shall be built in each provincial capital; civil and military officials serving in the provinces who are loyal, brave, and beloved by the people, and whom public opinion unanimously approves, shall receive sacrificial honors to encourage those still in office.

sentences.zh: 如將軍蔡良，提督張起雲，總兵蘇大有、魏翥國，足稱斯選。」

translations.literal: Such as General Cai Liang, Provincial Military Commander Zhang Qiyun, and Regional Commanders Su Dayou and Wei Zhuguo—fully worthy of this selection."
translations.idiomatic: Such as General Cai Liang, Provincial Military Commander Zhang Qiyun, and Regional Commanders Su Dayou and Wei Zhuguo—fully worthy of this honor."

sentences.zh: 定制，春、秋祭日視京師，以知府承祭，品物儀節亦如之。

translations.literal: By regulation the spring and autumn sacrifice days followed those of the capital; the prefect presided over the sacrifice, and the offerings and ritual procedures were likewise the same.
translations.idiomatic: By regulation the spring and autumn sacrifice days followed those of the capital; the prefect presided, and the offerings and ritual procedures were the same.

sentences.zh: 功臣專祠，詔為孔有德建祠，度地彰義門外三里，曰定南武壯王祠，二妃祔焉，

translations.literal: Dedicated temples for meritorious officials. An edict ordered a temple built for Kong Youde; a site three li outside Zhangyi Gate was measured out, named the Temple of Prince Dingnanwuzhuang, and his two consorts were enshrined alongside him.
translations.idiomatic: Dedicated temples for meritorious officials. An edict ordered a temple built for Kong Youde; a site three li outside Zhangyi Gate was chosen and named the Temple of Prince Dingnanwuzhuang, with his two consorts enshrined alongside him.

sentences.zh: 定春、秋展祀，其後建恪僖公祠安定門外，祀一等公遏必隆並縣?舒舒覺羅氏。

translations.literal: Spring and autumn sacrifices were established; later the Temple of Duke Kexi was built outside Anding Gate to enshrine Duke of the First Rank Ebilun and his consort of the Sushu Gioro clan.
translations.idiomatic: Spring and autumn sacrifices were established; later the Temple of Duke Kexi was built outside Anding Gate to enshrine Duke of the First Rank Ebilun and his consort of the Sushu Gioro clan.

sentences.zh: 嗣領侍衛內大臣尹德，尚書阿里袞暨其夫人，乾隆時並祔祀雲。

translations.literal: Subsequently Chief Grand Minister Yinde, Minister Aligun and his wife were also enshrined in attendance during the Qianlong reign.
translations.idiomatic: Later Chief Grand Minister Yinde, Minister Aligun, and his wife were also added to the temple during the Qianlong reign.

sentences.zh: 其建自雍正朝者，朝陽門外勤襄公祠，祀定南將軍佟圖賴及其夫人，長子忠勇國綱、次子端純國維，皆以軍功祔祀。

translations.literal: Those built from the Yongzheng reign included the Temple of Duke Qinxiang outside Chaoyang Gate, enshrining Regional Commander of Dingnan Tuntu Lai and his wife, the eldest son Zhongyong Guogang and the second son Duanchun Guowei—all enshrined in attendance for military merit.
translations.idiomatic: Temples built from the Yongzheng reign included the Temple of Duke Qinxiang outside Chaoyang Gate, honoring Regional Commander of Dingnan Tuntu Lai and his wife, along with his eldest son Zhongyong Guogang and second son Duanchun Guowei—all enshrined for their military service.

sentences.zh: 德勝門外文襄公祠，祀大學士圖海。

translations.literal: Outside Desheng Gate is the Temple of Duke Wenxiang, enshrining Grand Secretary Tu Hai.
translations.idiomatic: Outside Desheng Gate stands the Temple of Duke Wenxiang, dedicated to Grand Secretary Tu Hai.

sentences.zh: 安定門外與恪僖祠並峙者，為弘毅公祠，祀光祿大夫額亦都，並以夫人配。

translations.literal: Outside Anding Gate, standing alongside the Temple of Duke Kexi, is the Temple of Duke Hongyi, enshrining Grand Master of Splendid Happiness Ebidu, with his wife enshrined alongside.
translations.idiomatic: Outside Anding Gate, beside the Temple of Duke Kexi, stands the Temple of Duke Hongyi, honoring Grand Master of Splendid Happiness Ebidu and his consort.

sentences.zh: 建自乾隆朝者，東安門外恪僖公祠，祀內大臣哈世屯及其夫人，子承恩公米思翰、孫李榮保，其後曾孫大學士傅恆祔祀焉。

translations.literal: Those built in the Qianlong reign included the Temple of Duke Kexi outside Dong'an Gate, enshrining Grand Minister Hashitun and his wife, his son Duke Chengen Misihan and grandson Li Rongbao; later their great-grandson Grand Secretary Fu Heng was also enshrined in attendance.
translations.idiomatic: Built in the Qianlong reign was the Temple of Duke Kexi outside Dong'an Gate, honoring Grand Minister Hashitun and his wife, his son Duke Chengen Misihan and grandson Li Rongbao; later their great-grandson Grand Secretary Fu Heng was added as well.

sentences.zh: 崇文門內雙忠祠，祀左都御史拉布敦、都統傅清。

translations.literal: Inside Chongwen Gate is the Temple of Double Loyalty, enshrining Censor-in-Chief of the Left Labudun and Commander-in-Chief Fu Qing.
translations.idiomatic: Inside Chongwen Gate stands the Temple of Double Loyalty, dedicated to Censor-in-Chief of the Left Labudun and Commander-in-Chief Fu Qing.

sentences.zh: 合昭忠、賢良而復建專祠者，他無與比也。

translations.literal: Those who were enshrined in both the Temple of Manifest Loyalty and the Temple of Worthies and then received dedicated temples again had no parallel.
translations.idiomatic: Those honored in both the Temple of Manifest Loyalty and the Temple of Worthies who then received their own dedicated temples were unmatched in this regard.

sentences.zh: 地安門外旌勇祠，祀將軍明瑞，而都統扎拉豐阿，統領觀音保，總兵李全、王玉廷、德福亦先後入祔。

translations.literal: Outside Di'an Gate is the Temple of Commended Valor, enshrining General Mingrui; Commanders-in-Chief Zhalafeng'a and Guanyinbao, and Regional Commanders Li Quan, Wang Yuting, and Defu were also subsequently enshrined in attendance.
translations.idiomatic: Outside Di'an Gate stands the Temple of Commended Valor, dedicated to General Mingrui; Commanders-in-Chief Zhalafeng'a and Guanyinbao and Regional Commanders Li Quan, Wang Yuting, and Defu were later added as well.

sentences.zh: 睿忠親王祠在朝陽門外，祀多爾袞並福晉六人。

translations.literal: The Temple of Prince Ruizhong is outside Chaoyang Gate, enshrining Dorgon and six consorts.
translations.idiomatic: Outside Chaoyang Gate stands the Temple of Prince Ruizhong, honoring Dorgon and six of his consorts.

sentences.zh: 嘉慶時，建大學士福康安祠曰「獎忠」，在東安門外，都統額勒登保祠曰「褒忠」，在地安門外。

translations.literal: In the Jiaqing period a temple for Grand Secretary Fukang'an was built, named "Commending Loyalty," outside Dong'an Gate; a temple for Commander-in-Chief Ele Dengbao was named "Praising Loyalty," outside Di'an Gate.
translations.idiomatic: During the Jiaqing reign a temple for Grand Secretary Fukang'an called "Commending Loyalty" was built outside Dong'an Gate, and a temple for Commander-in-Chief Ele Dengbao called "Praising Loyalty" outside Di'an Gate.

sentences.zh: 光緒時，建科爾沁親王僧格林沁祠曰「顯忠」，在安定門內。

translations.literal: In the Guangxu period a temple for Prince Sengge Rinchen of Khorchin was built, named "Manifest Loyalty," inside Anding Gate.
translations.idiomatic: During the Guangxu reign a temple for Khorchin Prince Sengge Rinchen called "Manifest Loyalty" was built inside Anding Gate.

sentences.zh: 大學士、伯李鴻章祠曰「表忠」，在崇文門內。

translations.literal: A temple for Grand Secretary and Earl Li Hongzhang was named "Commending Loyalty," inside Chongwen Gate.
translations.idiomatic: A temple for Grand Secretary and Earl Li Hongzhang called "Commending Loyalty" stood inside Chongwen Gate.

sentences.zh: 宣統時，合祀立山、聯元祠在宣武門外。

translations.literal: In the Xuantong period a combined temple for Lishan and Lian Yuan was built outside Xuanwu Gate.
translations.idiomatic: In the Xuantong reign a combined temple for Lishan and Lian Yuan was erected outside Xuanwu Gate.

sentences.zh: 凡京師專祠，歲春、秋仲月吉日，遣太常卿分往致祭。

translations.literal: For all dedicated temples in the capital, on an auspicious day in the second month of spring and autumn the Director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices was dispatched in turn to perform the sacrifice.
translations.idiomatic: For all dedicated temples in the capital, on an auspicious day in the second month of spring and of autumn the Director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices was sent to conduct the sacrifice.

sentences.zh: 用少牢一、果品五。

translations.literal: The lesser tai lao was used once, with five trays of fruit.
translations.idiomatic: Offerings consisted of one lesser tai lao and five trays of fruit.

sentences.zh: 唯佟圖賴、哈世屯兩祠，則少牢三，果品十有五。

translations.literal: Only at the temples of Tuntu Lai and Hashitun were three lesser tai lao used, with fifteen trays of fruit.
translations.idiomatic: Only at the temples of Tuntu Lai and Hashitun were three lesser tai lao offered, with fifteen trays of fruit.

sentences.zh: 旌勇祠少牢如通常，果品亦十五雲。

translations.literal: At the Temple of Commended Valor the lesser tai lao followed the usual practice, and the fruit offerings were also fifteen.
translations.idiomatic: At the Temple of Commended Valor the lesser tai lao followed the usual practice, with fifteen trays of fruit as well.

sentences.zh: 位各用帛一、爵三，諸祠並同。

translations.literal: At each position one piece of silk and three libation cups were used; all temples were the same.
translations.idiomatic: Each position had one piece of silk and three libation vessels; the arrangement was the same at all temples.

sentences.zh: 嘉慶七年，始定承祭官行禮用蟒袍補服。

translations.literal: In the seventh year of Jiaqing it was first fixed that the presiding official should perform the rites in python robe with rank badge.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year of Jiaqing it was first established that presiding officials should wear python robes with rank badges when performing the rites.

sentences.zh: 其在各省者，歲春、秋守土官致祭。

translations.literal: In the provinces, local officials performed the sacrifices in spring and autumn.
translations.idiomatic: In the provinces, local officials conducted the spring and autumn sacrifices.

sentences.zh: 茲紀其勛勞最著者。

translations.literal: Here are recorded those whose meritorious service was most outstanding.
translations.idiomatic: Recorded here are those whose meritorious service was most distinguished.

sentences.zh: 自湖廣建忠節祠以祀左都督徐勇，各省建專祠始此。

translations.literal: Beginning with the Temple of Loyal Integrity built in Huguang to enshrine Left Regional Commander Xu Yong, dedicated provincial temples began from this point.
translations.idiomatic: Dedicated provincial temples began with the Temple of Loyal Integrity built in Huguang to honor Left Regional Commander Xu Yong.

sentences.zh: 康熙間，廣西建雙忠祠，祀馬雄鎮、傅弘烈，於是福建祀范承謨、陳啟泰、吳萬福、高天爵，雲南祀甘文焜。

translations.literal: In the Kangxi reign Guangxi built the Temple of Double Loyalty to enshrine Ma Xiongzhen and Fu Honglie; thereafter Fujian enshrined Fan Chengmo, Chen Qitai, Wu Wanfu, and Gao Tianjue, and Yunnan enshrined Gan Wenkun.
translations.idiomatic: During the Kangxi reign Guangxi built the Temple of Double Loyalty for Ma Xiongzhen and Fu Honglie; Fujian then honored Fan Chengmo, Chen Qitai, Wu Wanfu, and Gao Tianjue, and Yunnan honored Gan Wenkun.

sentences.zh: 雍正間，清河祀靳輔、齊蘇勒，開封祀田文鏡。

translations.literal: In the Yongzheng reign Qinghe enshrined Jin Fu and Qisuole, and Kaifeng enshrined Tian Wenjing.
translations.idiomatic: During the Yongzheng reign Qinghe honored Jin Fu and Qisuole, and Kaifeng honored Tian Wenjing.

sentences.zh: 盛京祀怡賢親王。

translations.literal: At Mukden Prince Yixian was enshrined.
translations.idiomatic: At Mukden Prince Yixian was honored.

sentences.zh: 乾隆中，詔通達、武功、慧哲、宣獻四郡王，禮烈、饒餘、鄭獻、穎毅四親王併入之，改名賢王祠。

translations.literal: During Qianlong an edict ordered the four princes of Tongda, Wugong, Huizhe, and Xuanxian, and the four princes of Lilie, Raoyu, Zhengxian, and Yingyi, all to be incorporated and the temple renamed the Temple of Worthy Princes.
translations.idiomatic: During Qianlong an edict incorporated the four princes of Tongda, Wugong, Huizhe, and Xuanxian and the four princes of Lilie, Raoyu, Zhengxian, and Yingyi into one temple, renamed the Temple of Worthy Princes.

sentences.zh: 已，睿忠、豫宣二親王，克勤郡王，亦均同祀。

translations.literal: Thereafter Prince Ruizhong, Prince Yuxuan, and the Prince of the Commandery of Keqin were all worshipped together.
translations.idiomatic: Later Prince Ruizhong, Prince Yuxuan, and the Prince of the Commandery of Keqin were all honored in the same temple.

sentences.zh: 嵇曾筠、高斌，合祀清河靳輔等祠。

translations.literal: Ji Zengyun and Gao Bin were jointly enshrined in the temple of Jin Fu and others at Qinghe.
translations.idiomatic: Ji Zengyun and Gao Bin were jointly honored in the Qinghe temple of Jin Fu and others.

sentences.zh: 伊犁祀班第、鄂容安，而拉布敦、傅清且建祠及西藏矣。

translations.literal: Ili enshrined Bandi and Erong'an, while Labudun and Fu Qing even had temples built in Tibet.
translations.idiomatic: Ili honored Bandi and Erong'an, and temples for Labudun and Fu Qing were even built in Tibet.

sentences.zh: 嘉慶時，武威建雙烈祠，祀韓自昌、韓加業，同安祀李長庚，成都祀德楞泰，韓城、滑縣祀強克捷。

translations.literal: In the Jiaqing period Wuwei built the Temple of Double Martyrs for Han Zichang and Han Jiaye; Tong'an enshrined Li Changgeng, Chengdu enshrined Delin Tai, and Hancheng and Huaxian enshrined Qiang Kejie.
translations.idiomatic: During Jiaqing Wuwei built the Temple of Double Martyrs for Han Zichang and Han Jiaye; Tong'an honored Li Changgeng, Chengdu honored Delin Tai, and Hancheng and Huaxian honored Qiang Kejie.

sentences.zh: 道光間，江南祀黎世序，台灣祀方振聲、馬步衢、陳玉威，趙城祀楊延亮，虎門祀關天培暨陳連升父子，鎮海祀裕謙，定海祀葛雲飛、鄭國鴻、王錫朋，京口祀海齡，寶山祀陳化成。

translations.literal: In the Daoguang period Jiangnan enshrined Li Shixu; Taiwan enshrined Fang Zhensheng, Ma Buqi, and Chen Yuwei; Zhaocheng enshrined Yang Yanliang; Humen enshrined Guan Tianpei together with Chen Liansheng and his son; Zhenhai enshrined Yu Qian; Dinghai enshrined Ge Yunfei, Zheng Guohong, and Wang Xipeng; Jingkou enshrined Hailing; and Baoshan enshrined Chen Huacheng.
translations.idiomatic: During Daoguang Jiangnan honored Li Shixu; Taiwan honored Fang Zhensheng, Ma Buqi, and Chen Yuwei; Zhaocheng honored Yang Yanliang; Humen honored Guan Tianpei and Chen Liansheng and his son; Zhenhai honored Yu Qian; Dinghai honored Ge Yunfei, Zheng Guohong, and Wang Xipeng; Jingkou honored Hailing; and Baoshan honored Chen Huacheng.

sentences.zh: 咸豐間，廣西祀長瑞、長壽暨阿爾精阿，西安、蘇州祀林則徐，安慶祀蔣文慶，廬州祀江忠源，瑞州祀劉騰鴻，江寧、蘇州祀向榮、張國樑，京口祀吉爾杭阿，附祀繃闊、劉存厚，揚州祀雙來、瞿騰龍，溧水、滸墅祀李坤元，天津祀佟鑒、謝子澄，長沙、九江祀塔齊布，湖廣、江西、安徽祀李續賓，江西、湖廣祀羅澤南，又與饒廷選合祀廣信，湘鄉復分祀澤南、王珍、劉騰鴻。

translations.literal: In the Xianfeng period Guangxi enshrined Changrui, Changshou, and Arjing'a; Xi'an and Suzhou enshrined Lin Zexu; Anqing enshrined Jiang Wenqing; Luzhou enshrined Jiang Zhongyuan; Ruizhou enshrined Liu Tenghong; Jiangning and Suzhou enshrined Xiang Rong and Zhang Guoliang; Jingkou enshrined Jierhang'a, with Bengkuo and Liu Cunhou enshrined in attendance; Yangzhou enshrined Shuang Lai and Qu Tenglong; Lishui and Xushu enshrined Li Kunyuan; Tianjin enshrined Tong Jian and Xie Zicheng; Changsha and Jiujiang enshrined Taqibu; Huguang, Jiangxi, and Anhui enshrined Li Xubin; Jiangxi and Huguang enshrined Luo Zinan, who was also jointly enshrined with Rao Tingxuan at Guangxin; and Xiangxiang separately enshrined Zinan, Wang Zhen, and Liu Tenghong.
translations.idiomatic: During Xianfeng Guangxi honored Changrui, Changshou, and Arjing'a; Xi'an and Suzhou honored Lin Zexu; Anqing honored Jiang Wenqing; Luzhou honored Jiang Zhongyuan; Ruizhou honored Liu Tenghong; Jiangning and Suzhou honored Xiang Rong and Zhang Guoliang; Jingkou honored Jierhang'a with Bengkuo and Liu Cunhou in attendance; Yangzhou honored Shuang Lai and Qu Tenglong; Lishui and Xushu honored Li Kunyuan; Tianjin honored Tong Jian and Xie Zicheng; Changsha and Jiujiang honored Taqibu; Huguang, Jiangxi, and Anhui honored Li Xubin; Jiangxi and Huguang honored Luo Zinan, also jointly honored with Rao Tingxuan at Guangxin; and Xiangxiang separately honored Zinan, Wang Zhen, and Liu Tenghong.

sentences.zh: 湖南、江西祀蕭啟江，湖廣祀胡林翼，後安慶亦祀之。

translations.literal: Hunan and Jiangxi enshrined Xiao Qijiang; Huguang enshrined Hu Linyi, who was later also enshrined at Anqing.
translations.idiomatic: Hunan and Jiangxi honored Xiao Qijiang; Huguang honored Hu Linyi, who was later honored at Anqing as well.

sentences.zh: 遵義祀羅繞典。

translations.literal: Zunyi enshrined Luo Raodian.
translations.idiomatic: Zunyi honored Luo Raodian.

sentences.zh: 同治間，湖北合祀官文、胡林翼，廬州祀李孟群，浙江祀瑞昌、王有齡、張玉良等，杭州祀羅遵殿，富陽祀熊建益，湖州祀趙景賢，陳州、安慶、臨淮、淮安祀袁甲三，南昌、青陽祀江忠義，安徽、湖廣祀李續宜，後復與多隆阿合祀潛山。

translations.literal: In the Tongzhi period Hubei jointly enshrined Guan Wen and Hu Linyi; Luzhou enshrined Li Mengqun; Zhejiang enshrined Ruichang, Wang Youling, Zhang Yuliang, and others; Hangzhou enshrined Luo Zundian; Fuyang enshrined Xiong Jianyi; Huzhou enshrined Zhao Jingxian; Chenzhou, Anqing, Linhuai, and Huai'an enshrined Yuan Jiasan; Nanchang and Qingyang enshrined Jiang Zhongyi; Anhui and Huguang enshrined Li Xuyi, who was later jointly enshrined with Dolonga at Qianshan.
translations.idiomatic: During Tongzhi Hubei jointly honored Guan Wen and Hu Linyi; Luzhou honored Li Mengqun; Zhejiang honored Ruichang, Wang Youling, Zhang Yuliang, and others; Hangzhou honored Luo Zundian; Fuyang honored Xiong Jianyi; Huzhou honored Zhao Jingxian; Chenzhou, Anqing, Linhuai, and Huai'an honored Yuan Jiasan; Nanchang and Qingyang honored Jiang Zhongyi; Anhui and Huguang honored Li Xuyi, later jointly honored with Dolonga at Qianshan.

sentences.zh: 安慶、蘇州、嘉興祀程學啟，河南、安徽、陝西、吉林祀多隆阿，後與林翼合祀安慶。

translations.literal: Anqing, Suzhou, and Jiaxing enshrined Cheng Xueqi; Henan, Anhui, Shaanxi, and Jilin enshrined Dolonga, who was later jointly enshrined with Lin Yi at Anqing.
translations.idiomatic: Anqing, Suzhou, and Jiaxing honored Cheng Xueqi; Henan, Anhui, Shaanxi, and Jilin honored Dolonga, later jointly honored with Lin Yi at Anqing.

sentences.zh: 江寧、安慶、吉安祀李臣典，湖南、福建、廣東祀張運蘭，曹州、天津、蒙城祀僧格林沁，後復祀奉天。

translations.literal: Jiangning, Anqing, and Ji'an enshrined Li Chengdian; Hunan, Fujian, and Guangdong enshrined Zhang Yunlan; Caozhou, Tianjin, and Mengcheng enshrined Sengge Rinchen, who was later also enshrined in Fengtian.
translations.idiomatic: Jiangning, Anqing, and Ji'an honored Li Chengdian; Hunan, Fujian, and Guangdong honored Zhang Yunlan; Caozhou, Tianjin, and Mengcheng honored Sengge Rinchen, later honored in Fengtian as well.

sentences.zh: 湖南、江蘇、安徽祀彭毓橘，湖廣祀曹仁美等，四川、湖南祀駱秉章，陝、甘祀劉松山，江寧、安慶祀馬新貽，江寧、湖南、湖北、安徽、直隸祀曾國籓，後復與國荃合祀開封。

translations.literal: Hunan, Jiangsu, and Anhui enshrined Peng Yuju; Huguang enshrined Cao Renmei and others; Sichuan and Hunan enshrined Luo Bingzhang; Shaanxi and Gansu enshrined Liu Songshan; Jiangning and Anhui enshrined Ma Xinyi; Jiangning, Hunan, Hubei, Anhui, and Zhili enshrined Zeng Guofan, who was later jointly enshrined with Guoquan at Kaifeng.
translations.idiomatic: Hunan, Jiangsu, and Anhui honored Peng Yuju; Huguang honored Cao Renmei and others; Sichuan and Hunan honored Luo Bingzhang; Shaanxi and Gansu honored Liu Songshan; Jiangning and Anhui honored Ma Xinyi; Jiangning, Hunan, Hubei, Anhui, and Zhili honored Zeng Guofan, later jointly honored with Guoquan at Kaifeng.

sentences.zh: 長沙合祀張亮基、潘鐸，巴燕岱祀穆克登額，哈密祀扎薩克親王錫伯爾，南豐祀吳嘉賓，貴州祀蔣霨遠、黃潤昌等。

translations.literal: Changsha jointly enshrined Zhang Liangji and Pan Duo; Bayandai enshrined Mukedeng'e; Hami enshrined the Jasak Prince Xiboer; Nanfeng enshrined Wu Jiabin; and Guizhou enshrined Jiang Weiyuan, Huang Runchang, and others.
translations.idiomatic: Changsha jointly honored Zhang Liangji and Pan Duo; Bayandai honored Mukedeng'e; Hami honored Jasak Prince Xiboer; Nanfeng honored Wu Jiabin; and Guizhou honored Jiang Weiyuan, Huang Runchang, and others.

sentences.zh: 於是禮部言：「各省專祠宜擇隙區曠土，毋侵民居，並禁改毀志乘名跡、聖賢祠墓。」

translations.literal: Thereupon the Ministry of Rites stated: "Dedicated provincial temples should be sited on open ground and must not encroach on private dwellings; alteration or destruction of landmarks recorded in local gazetteers, or temples and tombs of sages, is also forbidden."
translations.idiomatic: The Ministry of Rites then reported: "Dedicated provincial temples should be built on open ground without encroaching on private dwellings, and alteration or destruction of landmarks in local gazetteers or temples and tombs of sages is forbidden."

sentences.zh: 報可。

translations.literal: The report was approved.
translations.idiomatic: The report was approved.

sentences.zh: 光緒間，揚州、黃州祀吳文鎔，安徽、江西、閩、浙、甘肅祀劉典，江南、江西、福建、台灣祀沈葆楨，江蘇、建福、山東、湖南祀郭松林，江、浙、直隸、山東、河南祀吳長慶，後復祀朝鮮。

translations.literal: In the Guangxu period Yangzhou and Huangzhou enshrined Wu Wenrong; Anhui, Jiangxi, Fujian, Zhejiang, and Gansu enshrined Liu Dian; Jiangnan, Jiangxi, Fujian, and Taiwan enshrined Shen Baozhen; Jiangsu, Jianfu, Shandong, and Hunan enshrined Guo Songlin; Jiangsu, Zhejiang, Zhili, Shandong, and Henan enshrined Wu Changqing, who was later also enshrined in Korea.
translations.idiomatic: During Guangxu Yangzhou and Huangzhou honored Wu Wenrong; Anhui, Jiangxi, Fujian, Zhejiang, and Gansu honored Liu Dian; Jiangnan, Jiangxi, Fujian, and Taiwan honored Shen Baozhen; Jiangsu, Jianfu, Shandong, and Hunan honored Guo Songlin; Jiangsu, Zhejiang, Zhili, Shandong, and Henan honored Wu Changqing, later honored in Korea as well.

sentences.zh: 閩、浙、陝、甘、新疆、江寧祀左宗棠，四川、湖南、江西、安徽、江蘇祀鮑超，陝、甘、吉林祀金順，大理、鎮南祀楊玉科，江西、廣西、雲南、新寧祀劉長佑，雲、貴、廣西祀岑毓英，安徽、山東祀周盛波，後復與盛傳、戴宗騫合祀濟南。

translations.literal: Fujian, Zhejiang, Shaanxi, Gansu, Xinjiang, and Jiangning enshrined Zuo Zongtang; Sichuan, Hunan, Jiangxi, Anhui, and Jiangsu enshrined Bao Chao; Shaanxi, Gansu, and Jilin enshrined Jin Shun; Dali and Zhennan enshrined Yang Yuke; Jiangxi, Guangxi, Yunnan, and Xinning enshrined Liu Changyou; Yunnan, Guizhou, and Guangxi enshrined Cen Yuying; Anhui and Shandong enshrined Zhou Shengbo, who was later jointly enshrined with Shengchuan and Dai Zongqi at Jinan.
translations.idiomatic: Fujian, Zhejiang, Shaanxi, Gansu, Xinjiang, and Jiangning honored Zuo Zongtang; Sichuan, Hunan, Jiangxi, Anhui, and Jiangsu honored Bao Chao; Shaanxi, Gansu, and Jilin honored Jin Shun; Dali and Zhennan honored Yang Yuke; Jiangxi, Guangxi, Yunnan, and Xinning honored Liu Changyou; Yunnan, Guizhou, and Guangxi honored Cen Yuying; Anhui and Shandong honored Zhou Shengbo, later jointly honored with Shengchuan and Dai Zongqi at Jinan.

sentences.zh: 湖廣、江西、江寧、浙江西湖祀彭玉麟，荃，河南、安徽、湖北、直隸、甘、新祀張曜，安慶、江寧、青縣祀周盛傳，山東、江蘇祀陳國瑞，山東、陝西祀閻敬銘，湖南、甘、新祀劉錦棠，安徽、福建祀劉銘傳，山東、四川祀丁寶楨山東、陝西祀州、長沙、蘭州祀楊昌濬，江、浙、河南、直隸、山東祀李鴻章，直隸、奉天、河南、安徽祀宋慶，安徽及蘆台祀聶士成，湖南、江西、安徽、江寧祀劉坤一，廣西、雲、貴祀馮子材，安徽、湖南祀曾國華，甘、新祀陶模，直隸、安徽祀馬玉昆，安徽祀英翰，湖南、宣城祀鄧紹良，江南祀蕭孚泗，江寧祀陶澍、林則徐、鄒鳴鶴、福珠洪阿，清、淮、徐州祀吳棠，姚廣武等附之。

translations.literal: Huguang, Jiangxi, Jiangning, and West Lake in Zhejiang enshrined Peng Yulin; Sichuan, Henan, Anhui, Hubei, Zhili, Gansu, and Xinjiang enshrined Zhang Yao; Anqing, Jiangning, and Qingxian enshrined Zhou Shengchuan; Shandong and Jiangsu enshrined Chen Guorui; Shandong and Shaanxi enshrined Yan Jingming; Hunan, Gansu, and Xinjiang enshrined Liu Jintang; Anhui and Fujian enshrined Liu Mingchuan; Shandong and Sichuan enshrined Ding Baozhen; Shandong and Shaanxi enshrined Yan Jingming; Changsha and Lanzhou enshrined Yang Changjun; Jiangsu, Zhejiang, Henan, Zhili, and Shandong enshrined Li Hongzhang; Zhili, Fengtian, Henan, and Anhui enshrined Song Qing; Anhui and Lutai enshrined Nie Shicheng; Hunan, Jiangxi, Anhui, and Jiangning enshrined Liu Kunyi; Guangxi, Yunnan, and Guizhou enshrined Feng Zicai; Anhui and Hunan enshrined Zeng Guohua; Gansu and Xinjiang enshrined Tao Mo; Zhili and Anhui enshrined Ma Yukun; Anhui enshrined Ying Han; Hunan and Xuancheng enshrined Deng Shaoliang; Jiangnan enshrined Xiao Fusi; Jiangning enshrined Tao Shu, Lin Zexu, Zou Minghe, and Fuzhu Hong'a; Qingjiang, Huai'an, and Xuzhou enshrined Wu Tang, with Yao Guangwu and others enshrined in attendance.
translations.idiomatic: Huguang, Jiangxi, Jiangning, and West Lake in Zhejiang honored Peng Yulin; Sichuan, Henan, Anhui, Hubei, Zhili, Gansu, and Xinjiang honored Zhang Yao; Anqing, Jiangning, and Qingxian honored Zhou Shengchuan; Shandong and Jiangsu honored Chen Guorui; Shandong and Shaanxi honored Yan Jingming; Hunan, Gansu, and Xinjiang honored Liu Jintang; Anhui and Fujian honored Liu Mingchuan; Shandong and Sichuan honored Ding Baozhen; Changsha and Lanzhou honored Yang Changjun; Jiangsu, Zhejiang, Henan, Zhili, and Shandong honored Li Hongzhang; Zhili, Fengtian, Henan, and Anhui honored Song Qing; Anhui and Lutai honored Nie Shicheng; Hunan, Jiangxi, Anhui, and Jiangning honored Liu Kunyi; Guangxi, Yunnan, and Guizhou honored Feng Zicai; Anhui and Hunan honored Zeng Guohua; Gansu and Xinjiang honored Tao Mo; Zhili and Anhui honored Ma Yukun; Anhui honored Ying Han; Hunan and Xuancheng honored Deng Shaoliang; Jiangnan honored Xiao Fusi; Jiangning honored Tao Shu, Lin Zexu, Zou Minghe, and Fuzhu Hong'a; Qingjiang, Huai'an, and Xuzhou honored Wu Tang, with Yao Guangwu and others in attendance.

sentences.zh: 徐州祀滕學義、唐定奎，淮安祀張之萬，杭州祀阮元、蔣益澧，淮、揚祀章合才，南昌祀吳坤修，東鄉祀羅思舉，河南祀倭仁，溫縣祀李棠階，西安祀劉蓉、曾望顏，天津祀怡賢親王、文謙、丁壽昌，靈壽、保定祀成肇麟，順天薊州祀吳可讀，寶坻祀潘祖廕，新疆祀金運昌，奉天建三賢祠，祀文祥、崇實、都興阿，又祀左寶貴、依克唐阿、長順。

translations.literal: Xuzhou enshrined Teng Xueyi and Tang Dingkui; Huai'an enshrined Zhang Zhiwan; Hangzhou enshrined Ruan Yuan and Jiang Yili; Huai'an and Yangzhou enshrined Zhang Hecai; Nanchang enshrined Wu Kunxiu; Dongxiang enshrined Luo Siju; Henan enshrined Woren; Wenxian enshrined Li Tangjie; Xi'an enshrined Liu Rong and Zeng Wangyan; Tianjin enshrined Prince Yixian, Wen Qian, and Ding Shouchang; Lingshou and Baoding enshrined Cheng Zhaolin; Shuntian and Jizhou enshrined Wu Kedu; Baodi enshrined Pan Zuyin; Xinjiang enshrined Jin Yunchang; Fengtian built the Temple of Three Worthies for Wen Xiang, Chongshi, and Duxing'a, and also enshrined Zuo Baogui, Yiketang'a, and Changshun.
translations.idiomatic: Xuzhou honored Teng Xueyi and Tang Dingkui; Huai'an honored Zhang Zhiwan; Hangzhou honored Ruan Yuan and Jiang Yili; Huai'an and Yangzhou honored Zhang Hecai; Nanchang honored Wu Kunxiu; Dongxiang honored Luo Siju; Henan honored Woren; Wenxian honored Li Tangjie; Xi'an honored Liu Rong and Zeng Wangyan; Tianjin honored Prince Yixian, Wen Qian, and Ding Shouchang; Lingshou and Baoding honored Cheng Zhaolin; Shuntian and Jizhou honored Wu Kedu; Baodi honored Pan Zuyin; Xinjiang honored Jin Yunchang; Fengtian built the Temple of Three Worthies for Wen Xiang, Chongshi, and Duxing'a, and also honored Zuo Baogui, Yiketang'a, and Changshun.

sentences.zh: 吉林祀金福、延茂、富俊、希元，福建台灣祀王凱泰，四川西充祀武肅親王豪格，臨桂祀陳宏謀，貴陽祀曾璧光、韓起、黎培敬。

translations.literal: Jilin enshrined Jin Fu, Yanmao, Fujun, and Xiyuan; Fujian and Taiwan enshrined Wang Kaitai; Xichong in Sichuan enshrined Prince Wusu Haoge; Lingui enshrined Chen Hongmou; Guiyang enshrined Zeng Biguang, Han Qi, and Li Peijing.
translations.idiomatic: Jilin honored Jin Fu, Yanmao, Fujun, and Xiyuan; Fujian and Taiwan honored Wang Kaitai; Xichong in Sichuan honored Prince Wusu Haoge; Lingui honored Chen Hongmou; Guiyang honored Zeng Biguang, Han Qi, and Li Peijing.

sentences.zh: 於時各省紛請立專祠，諭毋濫。

translations.literal: At this time the provinces repeatedly requested dedicated temples; an edict forbade indiscriminate approval.
translations.idiomatic: At this time provinces repeatedly petitioned for dedicated temples; the court ordered that approval not be granted indiscriminately.

sentences.zh: 宣統享國未久，而湖北、安徽、陝、甘、奉天祀雷正綰，直隸、山東、河南、安徽祀程文炳，安徽及蒙古旗祀潘萬才，合肥祀董履高，渦陽祀牛師韓，杭州西湖祀徐用儀、許景澄、袁昶，號為「三忠」云。

translations.literal: The Xuantong reign was brief, yet Hubei, Anhui, Shaanxi, Gansu, and Fengtian enshrined Lei Zhengwan; Zhili, Shandong, Henan, and Anhui enshrined Cheng Wenbing; Anhui and the Mongol Banners enshrined Pan Wancai; Hefei enshrined Dong Lugao; Guoyang enshrined Niu Shihan; West Lake in Hangzhou enshrined Xu Yongyi, Xu Jingcheng, and Yuan Chang, known as the "Three Loyal Ones."
translations.idiomatic: Though the Xuantong reign was brief, Hubei, Anhui, Shaanxi, Gansu, and Fengtian honored Lei Zhengwan; Zhili, Shandong, Henan, and Anhui honored Cheng Wenbing; Anhui and the Mongol Banners honored Pan Wancai; Hefei honored Dong Lugao; Guoyang honored Niu Shihan; West Lake in Hangzhou honored Xu Yongyi, Xu Jingcheng, and Yuan Chang, known as the "Three Loyal Ones."

sentences.zh: 昶又祀蕪湖。

translations.literal: Yuan Chang was also enshrined at Wuhu.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Chang was also honored at Wuhu.

sentences.zh: 自是聯元祀寶坻，張之洞祀武昌，王文韶祀長沙，馬維麒祀成都，丁體昌祀秦州，夏毓秀祀昆明，此皆舉其大者。

translations.literal: Thereafter Lian Yuan was enshrined at Baodi, Zhang Zhidong at Wuchang, Wang Wenshao at Changsha, Ma Weilin at Chengdu, Ding Tichang at Qinzhou, Xia Yuxiu at Kunming—these are the principal cases.
translations.idiomatic: Thereafter Lian Yuan was honored at Baodi, Zhang Zhidong at Wuchang, Wang Wenshao at Changsha, Ma Weilin at Chengdu, Ding Tichang at Qinzhou, and Xia Yuxiu at Kunming—the principal cases among them.

sentences.zh: 其餘疆吏題請，禮臣議覆，事載實錄，年月可稽者，尚不一而足也。

translations.literal: As for other petitions by frontier officials reviewed by the Ministry of Rites, matters recorded in the Veritable Records with ascertainable dates are still too numerous to count.
translations.idiomatic: Other petitions by frontier officials reviewed by the Ministry of Rites, with dates ascertainable in the Veritable Records, are still too numerous to count.

sentences.zh: 有清一代，從龍諸佐，蔚起關外。

translations.literal: Throughout the Qing dynasty, the founding assistants rose in great numbers beyond the pass.
translations.idiomatic: Throughout the Qing dynasty, founding assistants rose in great numbers from beyond the pass.

sentences.zh: 平三籓，漢將西北為多。

translations.literal: In pacifying the Three Feudatories, Han generals from the northwest predominated.
translations.idiomatic: In pacifying the Three Feudatories, Han generals from the northwest predominated.

sentences.zh: 靖三省教匪，蜀將競興。

translations.literal: In quelling the sectarian rebels of the three provinces, Shu generals flourished in competition.
translations.idiomatic: In suppressing the sectarian rebels across three provinces, generals from Shu rose in great numbers.

sentences.zh: 東南海寇橫，閩帥踵起。

translations.literal: When pirates ravaged the southeast seas, Fujian commanders arose in succession.
translations.idiomatic: When pirates ravaged the southeastern seas, commanders from Fujian arose one after another.

sentences.zh: 湘楚武臣，戡平粵亂。

translations.literal: Hunan and Hubei military men quelled the rebellion in Guangdong.
translations.idiomatic: Military men from Hunan and Hubei quelled the rebellion in Guangdong.

sentences.zh: 剿捻一役，參以皖將。

translations.literal: In the campaign against the Nian rebels, Anhui generals participated.
translations.idiomatic: In the campaign against the Nian rebels, Anhui generals played a major part.

sentences.zh: 其間完節死綏，祠祀尤夥。

translations.literal: Among them those who preserved their integrity and died in office were enshrined in especially great numbers.
translations.idiomatic: Those who preserved their integrity and died in office were honored with temples in especially great numbers.

sentences.zh: 其功臣總祠，世宗朝，建忠勇祠蘭州。

translations.literal: As for collective temples to meritorious officials, in the Shizong reign the Temple of Loyal Courage was built at Lanzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Collective temples to meritorious officials included the Temple of Loyal Courage built at Lanzhou in the Shizong reign.

sentences.zh: 仁宗朝，建彰忠祠喀什噶爾。
